29: Moderates have led the INC since 1885 with petition, prayer and press. By the early 1900s: no self-governance, no relief, no power. Extremists say gentle methods fail.
Lal-Bal-Pal and Sri Aurobindo lead. Tilak turned Ganapati 1893 and Shivaji 1896 festivals into political platforms: culture first, then political energy. Aurobindo and Pal want Purna Swaraj.
Curzon 99-05 hits local self-government (1899 Act), education (1904 Universities Act) and the press (1904 Official Secrets Act). Stronger villain, stronger hero.
Announced July 1905, effective 16 October 1905. Stated reason: good governance. Indian view: Divide and Rule. Nawab Salimullah welcomes it; Muslim League follows in 1906.
Press campaign by Surendranath Bannerjea and C.R. Das fails. The Partition still comes, so on 7 August 1905 the Moderates themselves pass the Boycott Resolution.
Extremists add Swaraj and Passive Resistance (NC + CD + CW) and take the movement beyond Bengal. At Barisal in April 1906 police stop the Bande Mataram badge procession: a big boost.
Boycott and Swadeshi, national education, TISCO (1907), Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company (1906), picketing, Samitis, Jatras, religious symbols, workers' strikes. Constructive Work builds Atmashakti.
Swadeshi goods are costly so the poor stay out; force and social boycott hit Lower Castes and Muslims; institutions are thin; Hindu symbols put Muslims off; British imports are not hit.
Calcutta 1906: Naoroji presides, four resolutions. Morley's hint at reforms makes Moderates shift the 1907 session to Surat. Rai versus Rash Behari Ghosh ends in shoes hurled, Extremists expelled.

Tilak to Mandalay (1908-14), Aurobindo retires, Pal retires, Rai abroad (1914-20). Leaderless, so Revolutionaries (1908-11) take over. Pen failed, People came out; People failed, guns; guns failed, MG.

Nationalism stays lit, mass politics begins, the Drain is explained, and the toolkit passes to Gandhi in 1920. Partition annulled at the December 1911 Delhi Durbar; the Muslim League's birth leaves communal politics.
30: By 1908 the movement is leaderless: Tilak in Mandalay, Aurobindo and Pal retired, Rai abroad. Pen failed, People came out; People failed, Guns came out; Guns failed, MG came out (1920+).
Long game: repeat 1857 through civil rebellion and army disaffection. Quick strike: assassinate hated officials to remove fear and arouse nationalism. A trial becomes a stage.
1902: Pramathanath Mitra founds the Anushilan Samiti, Calcutta. By 1906 an impatient inner circle forms round Barindra Kumar Ghosh's Jugantar. The British reply with the CID in 1903.
Jugantar: loose, propaganda of the deed. Dacca Anushilan (Pulin Behari Das, 1906): rigid, long-term, Repeat 1857. Savarkars turn Mitra Mela (1899) into Abhinav Bharat (1904).

VOICE: free speech, weapons despite the Arms Act 1878, killing officers in England, diplomatic pressure, NRIs. Savarkar in London, Hardayal in the USA, Shyamji's India House 1905, Cama's flag at Stuttgart, August 1907.
Dacca Anushilan loots the Zamindar of Barrah. At Muzzafarpur Chaki and Khudiram Bose miss Kingsford; two English women die. Chaki kills himself; Khudiram, 18, is executed: an instant martyr.
The Alipore Case brings mass arrests. C.R. Das defends Aurobindo and B.C. Pal refuses to testify, so he is not convicted and flees to Pondicherry. Barindra Kumar Ghosh goes to the Cellular Jail.
In Kesari, Tilak condemns Muzzafarpur violence but defends Chaki and Bose: oppression breeds violence. Charged with sedition, six years at Mandalay, with Jinnah defending him.
1909: Dhingra kills Curzon-Wyllie in London, who was not Curzon 99-05. Kanhere kills Jackson at Nasik with Savarkar's pistol. 1910: Savarkar gets transportation for life.
The Revolutionaries gave pride, and the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 tried to buy peace. In 1911 the Partition was annulled and Delhi became capital. Curzon 99-05 lost the map but won the plan.
1912: Rash Behari Bose bombs Hardinge 10-16 at Chandni Chowk; Hardinge survives. Ghadar 1913-15, Japan 1915, IIL 1942, first INA under Mohan Singh, then handed to Netaji in 1943.
31: Census 1881: Muslims about 20%, a majority in Punjab, about 50% in Bengal, told as one community. Reports on education, jobs and poverty by religion show Muslims behind Hindus.
Western education was costly and Bengal Muslims were poor ryots. Ulamas resisted it, some wished to keep Persian, landlords saw no use. So Hindus gained the new professions.
Divide & Rule is the tool of loot. Hunter 1871: appease Muslims. Job reservation 1897. Partition 1905: Muslim-majority East Bengal and Assam. All three favoured the elite.
Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (1817-98): India is many qaums; Muslims need Western education. MAO College 1875, Educational Congress 1886 rivals the INC. He drew the Two Nation blueprint.
Arya Samaj turns aggressive after Dayanand dies in 1883; Cow Killing Riots 1893; the INC does not condemn them. Hindi-Urdu quarrel (Hindi wins 1900) and Swadeshi symbols deepen Muslim alienation.
The Aga Khan leads elite Muslims to Viceroy Minto 05-10: keep the Partition, reservation by population, separate electorates. Separate electorates are the hinge: Muslims elect Muslims.
The Muslim League, Dacca, December 1906, holds the British to Simla promises. Green Book by Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Mohammed Ali Jauhar; London branch 1908 under Ameer Ali. A 13-year head start.
Unrest made the British run repression and reform together. Move 1 split the INC at Surat 1907; Move 2 divided Hindus and Muslims by separate electorates.
ICA 1909: ILC 69 (9 + 60: 27 elected, 33 nominated), official majority 37 against 32. First 'election', Sinha in the VEC. Morley: only Limited Self-Government.
Muslims got separate electorates in the ILC, PLCs and local bodies: 8 of 27 elected seats, about 30% against 20% population. Separate means a candidate of a Group, for a Group, by a Group.

ICA 1909 lasted only 10 years, the shortest. Moderates wanted real power, the goal was Swaraj, legislatures were powerless: a Benevolent Despotism. Minto 05-10, Father of Communal Electorate; communal politics hardened to 1947.
